new.title: CNF clause and occurrence costs for cyclic permission tables with hidden bits
new.statement:
∀ (n w a : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 2 ≤ n →
  let Pat := Fin (w+1) → Bool
  let Raw := Fin n × Pat
  let Cl := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum Raw (Fin a))
  let accepts := fun T : Raw → Bool => ∃ x : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
    T (i, fun j : Fin (w+1) => x ⟨(i.val+j.val)%n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
  let enc := fun F : Finset Cl => ∀ T : Raw → Bool,
    accepts T ↔ ∃ z : Fin a → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim T z) (↑F : Set _)
  let pos := fun C : Cl => (C.filter (fun l =>
    l.2 = true ∧ ∃ e : Raw, l.1 = Sum.inl e)).card
  let d := if n ≤ w+1 then n else w
  let ports := 2^(min n (w+1))
  let groups := 2^(min d a)
  let block := 2^(d-a)
  (∀ G : Finset Cl, enc G →
    groups * n^block ≤ G.card ∧ ports * n^block ≤ (∑ C ∈ G, pos C) ∧
      ∃ C ∈ G, block ≤ pos C) ∧
  (n ≤ w+1 → ∃ F : Finset Cl, enc F ∧ F.card = groups * n^block ∧
    (∑ D ∈ F, pos D) = ports * n^block ∧ (∀ D ∈ F, pos D ≤ block) ∧
    ∀ D ∈ F, ∀ e : Raw, (Sum.inl e, false) ∉ D)
new.unlocks: Prices the raw cyclic feasibility predicate against all existential CNF encodings.
new.context: For short windows choose a reversible width-w register with n-step identity and retain only patterns on its seed trajectories. Each seed has a disjoint switch in each row. Reconstruct the disjoint-block false-clause charging argument and the register construction from the definitions. A uniform word translation retains each realizable pattern with probability H/J, giving the occurrence bound. Full windows have disjoint blocks and attain all three bounds.

new.title: Exact field-linear parity scan width for cyclic binary affine feedback beyond two full routing blocks
new.statement:
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [CharP K 2] (b a m : ℕ),
  let w := b + 1
  let n := a + 1
  let Control := (Fin b → ZMod 2) × ZMod 2
  let cost := Nat.choose (2 * w) w - 2
  let atSite := fun k => Fin.ofNat (a + 1) k
  let count := fun (C : Fin n → Control) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → ZMod 2)).filter (fun x =>
      ∀ i : Fin n, x (atSite (i.val + w)) = x i + (C i).2 +
        ∑ j : Fin b, (C i).1 j * x (atSite (i.val + 1 + j.val)))).card
  let admits :=
    ∃ (s : Fin m → K) (step : Fin n → Control → (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K))
      (out : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] K),
      ∀ C : Fin n → Control,
        out ((List.finRange n).foldl (fun v i => step i (C i) v) s) = (count C : K)
  (cost ≤ m → admits) ∧ (2 * (2 * w - 1) ≤ n → admits → cost ≤ m)
new.unlocks: determines the number of field coordinates needed to count cyclic affine-feedback solutions in characteristic two
new.context: Cyclic words correspond to fixed seeds, including repeated sites on short cycles. Track the products of the linear row maps on every proper nonzero exterior degree, starting from their identity matrices. Left multiplication is linear and the sum of traces gives parity for every bias. Cut after 2w-1 rows when the suffix is at least as long. Both control blocks realize every affine permutation independently, so prefix states and suffix functionals factor the full affine fixed-point matrix. Its rank forces the same dimension.

new.title: Full-cube operand defects bound the ordinary rank of a fan-in-two one-hot predictor's sign matrix
new.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true]))
∀ (n m : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+m) C →
  let t := C.gates.countP nonlinear
  let raw := Fin (n+m) → Bool
  let W := fun (w : ℕ) (x : raw) => (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD w false
  let defect : Matrix (Fin (n+m+C.gates.length)) (raw × raw) (ZMod 2) := fun w v =>
    if (∃ g ∈ C.gates, nonlinear g = true ∧ w.val ∈ g.inputs) ∧
      xor (xor (W w.val v.1) (W w.val v.2))
          (xor (W w.val (fun i => xor (v.1 i) (v.2 i))) (W w.val (fun _ => false))) = true
    then 1 else 0
  let value := fun (a : Fin n) (b : Fin m) => C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach a b)
  let K : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) ℚ := fun i j => if value i j then -1 else 1
  let V := Fin (2*t) → ZMod 2
  2 * 4^defect.rank * K.rank ≤ (4^defect.rank + 1) * 4^t ∧
  (5 * 4^t < 8 * K.rank → defect.rank = 0 ∧
    ∃ (row : Fin n → V) (col : Fin m → V) (Q : Fin n → Bool) (R : Fin m → Bool),
      ∀ i j, value i j = xor (xor (Q i) (R j))
        (decide ((∑ b : Fin (2*t), row i b * col j b) = 1)))
new.unlocks: bounds the rational rank of one-hot predictions in terms of the full-cube additivity defects of the operand wires
new.context: Write each operand as a raw affine term plus earlier formal products. Its four-value additivity defect is the same combination of the earlier product defects, so r is bounded by the count d of products feeding later gates. On the promise, the sign table selects rows and columns of the full XOR decoder up to signs. Its rational rank is bounded by the Walsh support. Apply the source bound. Above 5/8 no source is possible, and an omitted final product kills 3/4. Polarize the surviving disjoint products. Allow 3 to 5 hours.

changed.title: Small success advantages for repeated cyclic count scans have different memory costs at prime and binary power moduli
changed.statement:
∀ (d n p k : Nat), 0 < d → 0 < p → 0 < k →
  let w := d+2
  let D := 2^w
  let M := 4^d
  let Q := 2^k
  2*(k*(2*w+(2^w-1))+w) ≤ n →
  let Row := Nat → Bool
  let total := fun (rows : Nat → Row) =>
    ((List.range (2^n)).filter (fun word => (List.range n).all (fun site =>
      let pat := (List.range (w+1)).foldl (fun (acc bit : Nat) =>
        acc ||| ((word.testBit ((site+bit)%n)).toNat <<< bit)) 0
      rows site pat))).length
  let run := fun (S : Nat) (start : Fin S)
      (step : Nat → Nat → Fin S → Row → Fin S) (table : Nat → Row) =>
    (List.range p).foldl (fun prev passId =>
      (List.range n).foldl (fun state siteId => step passId siteId state (table siteId)) prev) start
  let succeeds := fun (m S R a b : Nat) =>
    ∃ (init : Fin R → Fin S) (update : Fin R → Nat → Nat → Fin S → Row → Fin S)
      (output : Fin R → Fin S → Nat), ∀ input : Nat → Row,
        a*R ≤ b*((List.finRange R).filter (fun coin =>
          output coin (run S (init coin) (update coin) input) == (total input)%m)).length
  ((∀ j : Nat, j ≤ k →
      succeeds Q (2^(j*(D*((D+p-1)/p)+1))) (2^(k-j)) (2^j) Q ∧
      ∀ S R : Nat, 0 < R → succeeds Q S R (2^j) Q → 2^(j*M) ≤ 4*S^(2*p-1)) ∧
    ∀ prime S' R' : Nat, Nat.Prime prime → prime ≤ Q → 0 < R' →
      succeeds prime S' R' 2 prime → prime^M ≤ (prime-1)^2*S'^(2*p-1))
changed.unlocks: prices memory for beating uniform guessing in repeated cyclic counts at prime and power-of-two moduli
changed.context: Encode two k-bit endpoint matrices on tagged banks and guard two tag flips, padding the last reset by affine feedback. The cyclic count is their inner product. The 2p-1 state transfers partition the inputs for fixed random bits. Apply the divisor bound. At a prime only the trivial and primitive orders occur. For 2^k the orders below 2^j contribute at most 2^(j-1). The other terms decrease geometrically after removing the common transcript factor, since M>=4. For achievability batch seeds, compute the trace modulo 2^j and guess the remaining bits uniformly.

changed.title: A polynomial-size fan-in-two circuit finds jointly independent translation periods for three groups of binary quadratic tests
changed.statement:
∀ (n t h : ℕ) (owner : Fin t → Fin 3),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin n → F
  let Slots := Fin 3 × Fin h
  let inputs := 1+t*n+t*n*n
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (flag : Fin (inputs+C.size))
    (out : Slots → Fin n → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
    C.size ≤ 2^20 * (n+t+h+2)^10 ∧
    ∀ (l : Fin t → X) (a : Fin t → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F),
      let eval := fun (j : Fin t) (x : X) =>
        (∑ i : Fin n, l j i*x i) + ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ b : Fin n, a j i b*x i*x b
      let valid := fun v : Slots → X =>
        LinearIndependent F v ∧
        ∀ (j : Fin t) (s : Fin h) (x : X), eval j (x+v (owner j,s)) = eval j x
      let pack := fun row : X => List.ofFn (fun bit : Fin n => decide (row bit ≠ 0))
      let bits := [false] ++ (List.ofFn (fun linearRow => pack (l linearRow))).flatten ++
        (List.ofFn (fun quadRow => (List.ofFn (fun coord => pack (a quadRow coord))).flatten)).flatten
      let wire := fun i : Fin (inputs+C.size) => (C.wires bits).getD i.val false
      (wire flag = true ↔ ∃ v, valid v) ∧
      (wire flag = true → valid (fun slot pos => if wire (out slot pos) then 1 else 0))
changed.unlocks: Supplies the independent periods needed to turn three classes of key observations into three pair tables.
changed.context: Find each group's common polar radical by binary elimination. On that radical every test minus its constant is linear, so intersect these kernels to get the period space. Color a basis of each space. Independent selections with the required quotas exist exactly when the rank of each of the seven unions is at least its total quota, by the independent transversal theorem applied to repeated colors. Choose a basis vector whose contraction preserves the residual inequalities, reduce its quota and repeat. Unroll elimination, tie breaking and output as Boolean gates.

changed.title: Three distinct binary cylinders cover fewer than twice their individual size exactly for a consistent sunflower with single-site petals
changed.statement:
∀ (n k : Nat), 0 < k → k ≤ n →
  ∀ (scope pat : Fin 3 → Finset (Fin n)),
    (∀ i : Fin 3, (scope i).card = k ∧ pat i ⊆ scope i) →
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin 3 => (scope i, pat i)) →
    let u := 2^(n-k)
    let covered := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin n))).filter
      (fun x => ∃ i : Fin 3, x ∩ scope i = pat i)).card
    let core := scope 0 ∩ scope 1 ∩ scope 2
    let consistent := ∃ y : Finset (Fin n), ∀ i : Fin 3, y ∩ scope i = pat i
    (covered < 2*u ↔ consistent ∧ core.card+1 = k) ∧
      (covered < 2*u → 4*covered = 7*u)
changed.unlocks: classifies the exceptional triples needed to determine which dense cyclic tables can omit three entries
changed.context: Inconsistent assignments already contain a disjoint pair. For compatible assignments align their signs. A pair of scopes differing by a single exchange intersects in u/2 words; other distinct pairs intersect in at most u/4. With at most one exchange pair, inclusion-exclusion gives at least 2u. With exactly two, the middle scope lies in the union of the outer scopes, giving 2u. Three exchange pairs either fit in k+1 sites, giving 2u, or share a core of k-1 sites with distinct petals. The latter covers seven of the eight petal patterns.

changed.title: Two batches of word queries suffice for certified recovery of a hidden binary formula above a majority gap
changed.statement:
∀ (n s : ℕ), 3 ≤ s → s ≤ n →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let high := fun (G : F) =>
    2 ^ n * (2 ^ (s - 1) + 1) ≤
      2 ^ s * (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => sat G x = true)).card
  let L := Nat.clog 2 (n + 1)
  let q₁ := 16 * (1 + 4 * (1 + L)) + 4 * 2 ^ s
  let q₂ := 4 * s * (L + 4)
  ∃ M : ℕ, 0 < M ∧
    ∃ (first : Fin M → Fin q₁ → W)
      (second : Fin M → (Fin q₁ → Bool) → Fin q₂ → W)
      (report : Fin M → (Fin q₁ → Bool) → (Fin q₂ → Bool) → Option F),
      ∀ A : F,
        let result := fun seed : Fin M =>
          let a := fun i => sat A (first seed i)
          let b := fun j => sat A (second seed a j)
          report seed a b
        (∀ t B, result t = some B → high A ∧ ∀ z, sat B z = sat A z) ∧
        (high A → 3 * M ≤
          4 * (Finset.univ.filter (fun u : Fin M => (result u).isSome = true)).card)
changed.unlocks: gives the certified recovery cost of two batches of queries on the promised hidden binary formulas
changed.context: Use a strength-four calibration and independent uniform words together. Its positive pair hull handles two disjoint clauses or identifies a common literal half. Find a passing word on the opposite half. In batch two flip random subsets there, including each noncenter bit with probability 1/s. Remove every candidate appearing in a passing flip. Require each survivor to be alone among survivors in some failing flip. This certifies every forced bit. At most s-1 are forced on a high star, so each needed elimination or isolation has probability at least 1/(4s) per test. Union bound over the bits.

changed.title: Sparse answer transcripts bound randomized one-batch recovery of signed stars even with a known center
changed.statement:
∀ (b r : ℕ), 0 < r → r ≤ b →
  let W := Bool × (Fin b → Bool)
  let P := Fin b → Option Bool
  let fam := (Finset.univ : Finset P).filter (fun v =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin b => (v i).isSome = true)).card = r)
  let star := fun (p : P) (x : W) => decide
    (x.1 = true ∨ ∀ i : Fin b, p i = none ∨ p i = some (x.2 i))
  let N := Nat.choose b r
  let K := 2 ^ r
  ∀ (M q : ℕ), 0 < M →
    ∀ (ask : Fin M → Fin q → W) (report : Fin M → (Fin q → Bool) → Option (W → Bool)),
      let H := ∑ p ∈ fam, (Finset.univ.filter (fun seed : Fin M =>
        report seed (fun j => star p (ask seed j)) = some (star p))).card
      (∀ v : ℕ, 0 < v →
        H ^ H * v ^ (q * H) ≤
          M ^ H * (v + 1) ^ (q * H) * v ^ (M * q * N)) ∧
      (3 * M * (K * N) ≤ 4 * H →
        (2 ^ (r - 1) * N) ^ (3 * K) ≤ 2 ^ ((4 * r + 6) * q))

changed.title: An adaptive learner certifies the whole hidden binary formula above a majority gap using a rare witness and subset tests
changed.statement:
∀ (n s : ℕ), 3 ≤ s → s ≤ n →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let high := fun (G : F) =>
    2 ^ n * (2 ^ (s - 1) + 1) ≤
      2 ^ s * (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => sat G x = true)).card
  let q := 16 * (1 + 4 * (1 + Nat.clog 2 (n + 1))) + 2 ^ s +
    s * (2 + Nat.clog 2 ((n + s - 1) / s))
  let Tape := Fin (2 ^ s) → W
  ∃ (ask : Tape → List Bool → W) (report : Tape → List Bool → Option F), ∀ A : F,
    let result := fun seed : Tape =>
      let history := (List.range q).foldl (fun (past : List Bool) _ =>
        past ++ [sat A (ask seed past)]) []
      report seed history
    (∀ t B, result t = some B → high A ∧ ∀ z, sat B z = sat A z) ∧
    (high A → 3 * Fintype.card Tape ≤
      4 * (Finset.univ.filter (fun u : Tape => (result u).isSome = true)).card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the total adaptive word queries for certified recovery of hidden binary formulas under the majority gap
changed.context: Query a strength-four covering pool and take the positive pair hull H. If H contains no literal half, a high input must have two disjoint clauses and H is exact. Return H only if high. If H contains a literal half, so does the input. Its opposite branch is empty or one subcube. Probe that branch 2^s times for a positive word. Flipping a subset of its bits now tests whether it meets the forced coordinates. Split into at most s blocks, binary search one hit at a time, and retest the rest. Return only after exhausting the blocks with at most s-1 hits.

changed.title: The first answer differing from a unary baseline bounds adaptive recovery of signed stars by both search time and remaining transcript capacity
changed.statement:
∀ (b r : ℕ), 0 < r → r ≤ b →
  let W := Bool × (Fin b → Bool)
  let P := Fin b → Option Bool
  let fam := (Finset.univ : Finset P).filter (fun v =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin b => (v i).isSome = true)).card = r)
  let star := fun (p : P) (x : W) => decide
    (x.1 = true ∨ ∀ i : Fin b, p i = none ∨ p i = some (x.2 i))
  let N := Nat.choose b r
  ∀ (M q : ℕ), 0 < M →
    ∀ (ask : Fin M → List Bool → W) (report : Fin M → List Bool → Option (W → Bool)),
      let output := fun (f : W → Bool) (seed : Fin M) =>
        let history := (List.range q).foldl (fun (past : List Bool) _ =>
          past ++ [f (ask seed past)]) []
        report seed history
      let hits := ∑ p ∈ fam, (Finset.univ.filter (fun t : Fin M =>
        output (star p) t = some (star p))).card
      let guesses := (Finset.univ.filter (fun u : Fin M =>
        (output (fun z : W => z.1) u).isSome = true)).card
      fam.card = N * 2 ^ r ∧
      hits ≤ guesses + M * (∑ j ∈ Finset.range q, min N (2 ^ j)) ∧
      (3 * M * fam.card ≤ 4 * hits →
        3 * 2 ^ r + 4 * Nat.clog 2 N ≤ 4 * (q + 2))
changed.unlocks: prices adaptive star recovery using both the time to find a differing answer and the number of remaining answer transcripts
changed.context: Trace each seed on the unary center predicate. An identical transcript can correctly name at most one star, and none if it abstains. At the initial different answer the query has rare center. For each r-subset of leaves only one sign pattern could hit, giving at most N targets. With j answers left, at most 2^j can be identified. Sum the smaller counts over initial hits. For L=ceil(log2 N), success 3/4 forces q>=L by the transcript count. The sum plus one is then 2^L+(q-L)N, and 2^L<=2N gives the additive bound.

changed.title: Complementary word queries decide a hidden binary majority gap with two-sided error using at most 1024 times two to the s queries
changed.statement:
∀ (n s : ℕ), 3 ≤ s → s ≤ n →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let Q := 2 ^ n
  let B := 4 * 2 ^ (s - 1)
  ∀ A : F,
    let N := (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => sat A x = true)).card
    let vote := fun (batch : Fin B → W) =>
      (List.ofFn batch).foldr (fun z rest =>
        let b := sat A z
        if b = sat A (fun i => !(z i)) then b else rest) false
    let hits := (Finset.univ.filter (fun tape : Fin 256 → Fin B → W =>
      144 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col : Fin 256 => vote (tape col) = true)).card)).card
    let total := Q ^ (256 * B)
    (2 * N ≤ Q → 4 * hits ≤ total) ∧
      (Q * (2 ^ (s - 1) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ s * N → 3 * total ≤ 4 * hits)
changed.unlocks: decides the promised hidden majority gap with the stated two-sided error and query budget
changed.context: Let u,v be the probabilities both words pass or both fail. Below or at half, u<=v. Above the gap the only forms are full, a signed star on at most s bits, or two disjoint clauses. On the star v=0 and u>=2^(1-s). Two disjoint clauses give u=1/4,v=1/8. Hence high inputs have u>=2v and u+v>=2^(1-s). A batch sees an equal pair with probability at least 15/16 on high inputs. Its chance to vote high is then at least 5/8, versus at most half on low inputs. The sum of 256 votes has variance at most 64. Chebyshev at distance 16 gives error at most 1/4.

changed.title: Adaptive word queries for a hidden binary majority gap obey a seed-count tradeoff and pay a length cost for either one-sided error
changed.statement:
∀ (n s : ℕ), 3 ≤ s → s ≤ n →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let count := fun (G : F) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun u => sat G u = true)).card
  let Q := 2 ^ n
  ∀ (M q fp fn : ℕ), fp + fn < M →
    ∀ (ask : Fin M → List Bool → W) (report : Fin M → List Bool → Bool),
      let yes := fun (A : F) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun seed : Fin M =>
        let history := (List.range q).foldl (fun (past : List Bool) _ =>
          past ++ [sat A (ask seed past)]) []
        report seed history = true)).card
      (∀ A : F, 2 * count A ≤ Q → yes A ≤ fp) →
      (∀ A : F, Q * (2 ^ (s - 1) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ s * count A → M ≤ yes A + fn) →
      2 ^ (s - 1) * (M - fp - fn) ≤ q * (M - fp) ∧
      (fn = 0 → 2 ^ (s - 3) * Nat.clog 2 (2 * (n - s + 2) + 2) ≤ q) ∧
      (fp = 0 → 2 * n + 2 ≤ 2 ^ q)
changed.unlocks: bounds seed counts and query lengths for adaptive hidden majority decisions with either one-sided error
changed.context: Trace each seed on a unary half cube. A star adds one rare pattern on the center and s-1 leaves. Among R rejecting seeds, at least R-fn must hit each pattern on the baseline path, whereas each path hits at most q patterns. Sum and use R>=M-fp. With fn=0 one rejecting path covers every leaf pattern on every s-1 leaves. Slice by s-3 leaves, then count distinct signed columns and constants. With fp=0 take an accepting path on the full cube. A constant column or two equal or complementary columns give a unary or binary half-cube predicate with identical labels.

changed.title: A two-state trace counts all nonzero Walsh transitions of the unmixed cyclic row and bounds both scheduled spacings at every width
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (s : ℕ) (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(s : I)) + x i + x (i+(s : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let pairs := fun (s : ℕ) => ∑ b : V,
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : V =>
      (∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix s x)))) ≠ 0)).card
  let A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ := fun src dst =>
    if src = 0 then (if dst = 0 then 1 else 4) else (if dst = 0 then 2 else 0)
  let total := Matrix.trace (A^k) +
    (if k % 2 = 1 then (2:ℤ)^(k-1) else -7*(2:ℤ)^(k-2))
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let h := if 3 ∣ k/g then 2*g else 0
  (pairs 0 : ℤ) = total ∧ (pairs d : ℤ) ≤ total ∧
    total ≤ (2:ℤ)^(2*h) * (pairs d : ℤ) ∧ (2:ℤ)^k * total ≤ 3*(7:ℤ)^k
changed.unlocks: Counts candidate products across each full shared-key transfer layer, including singular widths, and identifies the exponential cost of enumerating these products.
changed.context: In a cyclic mask with a zero, that zero resets the parity of the current run to even. A one switches parity, with weight four out of even and one out of odd. Any zero has weight one. The trace sums these walks, uniquely for each proper mask. On all ones it counts zero for odd k and twice 2^k for even k. Replace that contribution by 2^(k-gcd(k,2)). Sum the column bounds to allow singular mixing. Cayley-Hamilton gives T(k+2)=T(k+1)+8T(k), with T(0)=2 and T(1)=1. Induction gives T(k) ≤ 2*(7/2)^k and the odd correction fits one more (7/2)^k.

changed.title: An ordinary two-state integer matrix product computes one cyclic Walsh transition over all lifts of its input mask
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(d : I)) + x i + x (i+(d : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let lifts := fun (a : V) => Finset.univ.filter (fun u : V => mix u = a)
  let transfer := fun (u b : V) (j : ℕ) =>
    let i := (j : I)
    (fun (left right : B) =>
      sign ((u i+b i+b (i-2))*left + b (i-1)*left*right) : Matrix B B ℤ)
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  ∀ (a b : V),
    (∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix x)))) =
      ∑ u ∈ lifts a, Matrix.trace (List.prod (α := Matrix B B ℤ) ((List.range k).map (transfer u b))) ∧
    (lifts a).card = (if (∃ y : V, mix y = a) then
      (if 3 ∣ (k/g) then 4^g else 1) else 0)
changed.unlocks: Supplies the single-round character coefficients for the two scheduled words and their shared raw key, including widths at which the three-tap mix is singular.
changed.context: Expand the signed exponent on each cyclic edge. With each transfer typed as an integer matrix, matrix multiplication sums the shared Boolean state. Taking its trace closes the cycle. Sum over the lifts of the input mask. Orthogonality eliminates inconsistent masks. The three-tap recurrence on each d-orbit repeats u,v,u+v, giving four kernel words precisely when the orbit length is divisible by three.

changed.title: Sharp simultaneous prediction on binary permutations generated by one prefix shift and independent pair flips
changed.statement:
∀ w : ℕ,
  let K := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin w → K
  let V := X × K
  let I := V × Option (Fin w)
  let s := 2^w
  let coeff := V → Finset I → K
  ∀ p : Equiv.Perm V,
    let raw := fun (u : X) (b : X → K) (a : V) =>
      ((p a).1 + u, (p a).2 + b (p a).1)
    let bad := fun (c : coeff) (A : Finset V) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (X × (X → K))).filter (fun t =>
        let z := raw t.1 t.2
        let bit := fun j : I => j.2.elim (z j.1).2 (fun i => (z j.1).1 i)
        ∃ a ∈ A,
          (∑ S ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset I)).filter (fun S => S.card ≤ w),
            c a S * ∏ j ∈ S, bit j) ≠ (z a).2 * ∏ i : Fin w, (z a).1 i)).card
    let bound := fun (A : Finset V) =>
      2^s - 2^(s - (A.image (fun a => (p a).1)).card)
    (∀ (c : coeff) (A : Finset V), bound A ≤ bad c A) ∧
      ∃ c : coeff, ∀ A : Finset V, bad c A = bound A
changed.unlocks: The averaged all-permutation lower by counting, and an optimizer on each fixed base.
changed.context: At a fixed base the shift and all original-prefix flips are affine raw coordinates. Each occupied prefix x has error leading monomial (product of all shift bits) times b(x). The Heijnen-Pellikaan finite-grid footprint gives the union lower. For attainment prescribe error equal to the zero-shift indicator times b(x). The degree-w+1 term cancels from the predictor, including w=0. The same vector works for every marked subset.

changed.title: One packed cyclic nonlinear round agrees with every scalar lane for arbitrary input states and additive words
changed.statement:
∀ (k lanes gap : Nat) (hk : 0 < k), gap ≤ k →
  let word := Fin (2 ^ k)
  let atSite := fun j : Nat => (⟨j % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s x : Nat) =>
    ((x <<< (s % k)) ||| (x >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (raw : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc b =>
      acc ||| ((xor (raw.testBit b)
        (!(raw.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && raw.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
  ∀ (state addend : Fin lanes → word) (planes additions : Fin k → Nat),
    (∀ i w, (planes i).testBit w.val = (state w).val.testBit i.val) →
    (∀ i w, (additions i).testBit w.val = (addend w).val.testBit i.val) →
    let mix := fun j : Nat =>
      planes (atSite j) ^^^ planes (atSite (j + k - gap % k)) ^^^
        planes (atSite (j + gap))
    let full := 2 ^ lanes - 1
    ∀ (i : Fin k) (w : Fin lanes),
      (mix i.val ^^^ ((full ^^^ mix (i.val + 1)) &&& mix (i.val + 2)) ^^^
        additions i).testBit w.val =
      (step ((state w).val ^^^ rot gap (state w).val ^^^ rot (k - gap) (state w).val) ^^^
        (addend w).val).testBit i.val
changed.unlocks: Supplies the round induction in the scalar correspondence for all scheduled row and column certificate computations, independently of initial key-mask arithmetic.
changed.context: For each scalar rotation split the site below or above the reduced shift. Exactly one shifted part can contribute there and the width mask preserves the low bit. The two rotations read j-gap and j+gap cyclically. Reading a lane commutes with XOR and AND, and the full packed mask has a one there. In the scalar OR fold only the shifted Boolean at the requested site can set that bit. Apply the packed addend hypothesis last. The argument includes coincident neighbors. See packed-rounds.md at 1de61e3a54.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: The squared Frobenius error of the best rank-r approximation to a Hadamard matrix is n(n-r)
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ n →
    let err := fun (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) => ∑ i, ∑ j, (H i j - A i j)^2
    let best : ℝ := n * (n-r : ℕ)
    (∀ A, A.rank ≤ r → best ≤ err A) ∧ (∃ A, A.rank ≤ r ∧ err A = best)
changed.unlocks: Gives the attainable squared error under a rank constraint for an orthogonal sign target.
changed.context: All singular values of H are the square root of n, so the squared norm in discarded directions is n(n-r). Alternatively project onto the column space of any approximant for the lower bound, then keep r columns of H for equality.

changed.title: The truth tables of separate row-column probes determine the exact number of colors available for paired decoding
changed.statement:
∀ (n q : ℕ) (op : Fin q → Bool → Bool → Bool),
  let I := Fin n
  let rad := fun (f : Bool → Bool → Bool) =>
    let ones := ((Finset.univ : Finset (Bool × Bool)).filter (fun z => f z.1 z.2)).card
    if ones = 0 ∨ ones = 4 then 1 else if ones = 2 then 2 else 3
  let D := ∏ t : Fin q, rad (op t)
  ∀ (H : I → I → Bool) (π : Equiv.Perm I) (e : ℕ),
    (∃ (R C : Fin q → I → Bool) (out : Finset I → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool),
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (I × I)).filter (fun z =>
        out {z.1,z.2} (fun t => op t (R t z.1) (C t (π z.2))) ≠ H z.1 (π z.2))).card ≤ e) ↔
    ∃ label : I → Fin D,
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (I × I)).filter (fun z =>
        z.1 < z.2 ∧ label z.1 = label z.2 ∧ H z.1 (π z.2) ≠ H z.2 (π z.1))).card ≤ e
changed.unlocks: Gives the exact orientation resources of a parallel bank of arbitrary Boolean gates on separate row and column predicates.
changed.context: The orientation graph on four input types joins two types when exchanging their column bits changes the gate output. A constant has no edges. A balanced truth table is a nonconstant affine function, so the graph is complete bipartite according to its linear part. Every remaining table is AND with input and output complements, giving a triangle and an isolated type. Map each graph to a clique of its radix and represent every digit by a clique vertex. Combine digits independently. On a colliding pair pay exactly one error if its orientations disagree.

changed.title: One two-coloring splits many disjoint set families into two prescribed positive gains
changed.statement:
∀ (v n h : Nat), 0 < n → 2 ≤ h →
  let V := Fin v
  let P := Finset (Finset V)
  let gain := fun (p : P) => p.sum (fun s => s.card-1)
  ∀ fam : Fin n → P,
    (∀ i, (∀ s ∈ fam i, 2 ≤ s.card ∧ s.card-1 < h) ∧
      (∀ s ∈ fam i, ∀ u ∈ fam i, s ≠ u → Disjoint s u) ∧ gain (fam i) = h) →
    ∃ (red : Finset V) (redGain : Nat) (I : Finset (Fin n)),
      0 < redGain ∧ redGain < h ∧ n ≤ I.card * h * 4^h ∧
      ∀ i ∈ I,
        let left := (fam i).filter (fun s => s ⊆ red)
        let right := (fam i).filter (fun u => Disjoint u red)
        fam i = left ∪ right ∧ gain left = redGain ∧ gain right = h-redGain ∧
        (2*h < 3*redGain → left.card = 1) ∧
        (2*h < 3*(h-redGain) → right.card = 1)
changed.unlocks: Finds many columns respecting one two-coloring with the same two gains and singleton heavy sides.
changed.context: In each family isolate a set of weight at least h/3 if one exists, putting a weight above 2h/3 alone. Otherwise take sets until their sum first reaches h/3, staying below 2h/3. changed.title: Independent flips in symbol pairs bound simultaneous polynomial prediction on permutations of binary words
changed.statement:
∀ w : ℕ,
  let K := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin (w+1) → K
  let I := V × Fin (w+1)
  let s := 2^w
  ∀ (A : Finset V) (c : V → Finset I → K),
    let m := A.card
    let pred := fun (p : Equiv.Perm V) (a : V) =>
      ∑ S ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset I)).filter (fun S => S.card ≤ w),
        c a S * ∏ j ∈ S, p j.1 j.2
    let bad := (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm V)).filter (fun p =>
      ∃ a ∈ A, pred p a ≠ ∏ i : Fin (w+1), p a i)
    let total := 2^s * Nat.choose (2*s) m
    let empty := ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (s+1), Nat.choose s j * Nat.choose (2*j) m
    Nat.factorial (2*s) * (total - empty) ≤ s * total * bad.card
